order: Restore the in-house fresh-context adversarial reviewer as the primary review engine for both modes, and demote the external command-line engine to an optional cross-vendor layer — gate-class second opinions, or primary for projects that opt in. Pin that the primary brief carries the identical contract the external brief encodes: presume-broken discipline, independent re-verification through the project's verification manifest, inert-tier claims verified from the diff with a tier violation rated CRITICAL and forcing full depth, and the same verdict format under a REVIEW ENGINE header for auditability. Constrain the unavailable path to route the review to the primary reviewer rather than degrading, and make the in-session fallback last-resort — reachable only when no reviewer agent can run at all. Ship the new launcher brief and sync the harness document, the README trade-off wording, and the installer roster.
claims: Both briefs now encode the same contract, and the unavailable path routes to the primary reviewer instead of degrading. Syntax checks pass on the installer and all three hooks; the agent manifest reports 4 of 4 present, 0 missing; the primary brief's frontmatter parses with its model line intact; and the runner smoke test prints its usage line and the REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE verdict on the missing-binary path as designed. Independent re-verification is pinned by the restored rule. All green.
